reason: The hypothesis makes numerous specific claims about temperature-dependent structural evolution, dislocation behavior, and mechanical properties of a FeNiCrCoCu HEA coating, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the detailed, system-specific predictions made here.
premises: FeNiCrCoCu HEA coating maintains ordered FCC lattice and stable dislocation density up to 600 K
Above ~900 K, rapid lattice disorder occurs with reduced dislocation density and increased HCP atom fraction
Lattice disorder and HCP formation cause lattice softening, drop in hardness and wear resistance
Friction coefficient and tangential force increase above 900 K due to the deformation mechanism change
At ~600 K, modest dislocation density reduction can increase elastic modulus and maintain wear resistance
